Databricks

Source: vignettes/databricks.Rmd
databricks.Rmd

Databricks is a hosted data and analytics platform. Its SQL warehouses run queries against your tables. Query a Databricks SQL warehouse from Shiny using each visitor’s Databricks account. oauth_db_databricks() gives you a DBI connection for SQL or dbplyr queries.

The same sign-in works with brickster’s API functions, including warehouse listing and query submission.

Try the guided demo

For guided setup and an editable app, run this in the R console:

install.packages(c("brickster", "jsonlite", "processx", "askpass", "bslib"))
shinyOAuthDB::oauth_db_cloud_demo("databricks")

The launcher asks for your workspace URL and custom OAuth app registration. It uses SQL access with openid, profile, email, offline_access and sql scopes. A public PKCE registration needs no secret; a confidential registration uses masked input or OAUTHDB_DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET. Register the exact callback it prints, normally http://localhost:8100. This SQL demo requests narrower access than the all-apis preset below.

After sign-in, choose a SQL warehouse. If listing fails, enter its known warehouse ID or HTTP path from SQL Warehouses > your warehouse > Connection details. You need CAN USE on that warehouse. Click Run example query to run SELECT current_user() AS signed_in_user; listing warehouses doesn’t run SQL. Queries can start a stopped warehouse and consume compute credits. Stopping the local app leaves shared cloud compute running. Sign out and back in to choose a different warehouse after the first query.

Databricks Free Edition doesn’t provide the account-level custom OAuth registration this demo needs. Use a full workspace or eligible full-platform trial with access to custom registration. See the Free Edition limits and ?oauth_db_cloud_demo. For editing and resuming demos, see Getting started.

Register the app

In R, run install.packages("brickster") and ask your administrator to register a Databricks OAuth application with a client secret and http://localhost:8100 as its redirect URI. Allow the scopes requested by the preset, including all-apis and offline_access. Users need access to the workspace, warehouse, and data.

Save the client ID and secret in a local .Renviron file and restart R:

OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret

In the Databricks account console, an administrator opens Settings > App connections > Add connection. Register http://localhost:8100, allow All APIs for this preset and generate a client secret. Copy the ID and secret from the result; the secret can’t be retrieved later. These are custom OAuth connections, separate from service-principal machine credentials.

App value Where to find it
host Your workspace browser address, e.g. example.cloud.databricks.com
warehouse_id Workspace SQL Warehouses > your warehouse > Connection details; also the last part of its HTTP path
Client ID and secret The account console’s custom app connection

Give users CAN USE on the warehouse and the appropriate catalog, schema and table privileges. The cloud service can’t be reproduced by a local Docker demo.

A complete app

Save this as example.R. Replace the workspace host and copy the warehouse ID from the warehouse’s connection details:

library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

host <- "example.cloud.databricks.com"
client <- oauth_db_databricks_client(
  host = host,
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100"
)

ui <- oauth_ui(
  fluidPage(
    actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
    actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
    tableOutput("rows")
  ),
  id = "auth",
  client = client
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server("auth", client, auto_redirect = FALSE)
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())

  con <- oauth_db_databricks(
    auth$connection,
    host = host,
    warehouse_id = "warehouse-id"
  )

  output$rows <- renderTable({
    connection <- con()
    DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT current_user()")
  })
}

runApp(
  shinyApp(ui, server, uiPattern = ".*"),
  port = 8100,
  launch.browser = FALSE
)

# Open the app in your regular browser at http://localhost:8100
# (viewers in RStudio/Positron/etc. cannot perform necessary redirects)

Run source("example.R") and open http://localhost:8100. Sign in to run the query; signing out clears the output.

The query shows the Databricks user. Replace it with SQL for your tables. For dbplyr, get connection <- con() first, then pass it to dplyr::tbl().

Call brickster functions

To list warehouses, add verbatimTextOutput("warehouses") to the UI and this code inside server():

databricks <- oauth_db_databricks_api(auth$connection, host = host)

output$warehouses <- renderPrint({
  databricks$call(brickster::db_sql_warehouse_list)
})

Pass the function and its usual arguments to $call(). The client supplies the workspace host and the user’s current token.

For example, to use brickster’s query API, replace the table output with verbatimTextOutput("rows") and the render expression with:

output$rows <- renderPrint({
  databricks$call(
    brickster::db_sql_query,
    warehouse_id = "warehouse-id",
    statement = "SELECT current_user()",
    disposition = "INLINE",
    show_progress = FALSE
  )
})

This returns brickster’s query result. Use the DBI helper above when you want DBI::dbGetQuery() to return a data frame.

Connection options

Supply http_path = "/sql/1.0/warehouses/warehouse-id" instead of warehouse_id if you have the HTTP path. Set catalog and schema to choose SQL defaults; other connection options go to brickster.

Call con() before each operation. When its token changes, the helper replaces the connection. On sign-out or session end, con() stops returning the connection and calls the driver’s cleanup method. The brickster driver doesn’t invalidate retained native handles: a saved connection can still submit requests with its copied token. Keep using con() for each operation. See Getting started for results saved in the app.

Azure Databricks with Entra sign-in

For a workspace that accepts Microsoft Entra tokens, use an Entra Web app registration with delegated Databricks access. Set OAUTHDB_TENANT_ID and replace the client with:

client <- oauth_db_microsoft_client(
  services = "databricks_entra",
  tenant_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_TENANT_ID"),
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100"
)

Change host to the Azure workspace hostname and set auth_mode = "entra" on both oauth_db_databricks() and oauth_db_databricks_api().
